headline: Anthropic adds dynamic workflows in beta to Claude Managed Agents, with up to 1,000 agents per run
body: Anthropic says Claude Managed Agents can now use dynamic workflows, in beta: a workflow is a program that runs many agents in phases and combines their results. Anthropic caps a run at 64 agents working at once and 1,000 agents over the run's whole life. In Anthropic's testing, a single agent caught between 14 and 27 of 70 bugs per run while the workflow consistently hit 66, The Decoder reports.
note: For banks and insurers testing agent workloads, the token bill now sits next to the accuracy gain. The Decoder calls cost-effectiveness debatable, and Anthropic recommends starting small.

evidence.text: You can now let a Claude Managed Agents agent use dynamic workflows , in beta with the managed-agents-2026-04-01 beta header.
A workflow is a program that runs many agents in phases and combines their results.
Threads working at once in one run 64 The run creates no more until one finishes.
Agents a workflow starts over the run's whole life 1,000 When the workflow asks for more, the server doesn't start another agent, and the run ends with thread_limit_error .
Anthropic points to its own testing: The team hid 70 bugs in a 116,000-line codebase and found that a single agent caught between 14 and 27 per run, while the dynamic workflow consistently hit 66.
Whether this is cost-effective seems debatable.
Because these workflows can burn through "a lot of tokens," Anthropic recommends starting small.

correction: An earlier version said up to 1,000 sub-agents run in parallel, from The Decoder. Anthropic's documentation says 64 agents work at once in a run and 1,000 over the run's whole life, and the feature is in beta.
